Impl r1 for open-pr, per the approved plan (docs/phases/open-pr.md, r3). All changes are staged on phase-8/open-pr and uncommitted (base ede1dd1). No arbiter interjections.

What changed, where:
- src/bugalizer/git_ops/pull_request.py (new): slug parsing and canonical URL; env-only credential (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2, extraheader, empty credential.helper, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0); redaction; claim registry; per-project asyncio.Lock; leftover cleanup; reconcile (find PR -> owner via pushed_sha, then trailers, then explicit caller choice, else pr_unattributed; ls-remote resume via pushed_sha, otherwise branch_exists); fetch with --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head into refs/bugalizer/base/<id>; detached worktree; apply (-p1/-p0 from the headers); commit with trailers; push intent; guarded push; PR POST with a 422-already-exists re-lookup; atomic record. All git calls go through `_run_git`.
- db.py: claim_token plus the four proposal columns (schema and `_migrate`); try_claim_report(claim_token=); adopt_claim, release_claim (token CAS); fix_proposal_of_report; recorded_pull_request; fix_proposal_record_push_intent; record_pull_request, a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction split into _record_pr_proposal/_record_pr_report so a test can inject a failure mid-transaction; fix_analysis_for_proposal (tier and model for the PR body).
- models.py: FIX_APPROVED -> FIX_PROPOSED; OpenPrRequest (extra=forbid, so no branch field) and OpenPrResponse. CURRENT_PHASE_TARGETS is unchanged.
- api/reports.py: POST /reports/{id}/open-pr. Coded errors answer with a top-level {code, detail, ...}. An unexpected exception answers 500 internal_error with a redacted log line.
- config.py: github_token (SecretStr), commit author name and email, github_web_base, github_api_base. main.py: /health github_configured.
- Docs: .env.example, deploy-windows.md (git 2.29 minimum, token scope, new §7b with the codes table and the three branch_exists recoveries), decision log, roadmap, CLAUDE.md; scripts/windows/open-pr-smoke.ps1.

Deviations and additions to the plan, for review:
1. No FixProposalResponse model. GET fix_proposals still returns raw rows, which now include pr_url, pr_number, pushed_sha and pr_opened_at (asserted in a test).
2. Codes beyond the plan: 400 subcodes not_github / not_cloned / bad_default_branch / bad_id; 500 git_error for a local git failure (worktree add, commit); 500 internal_error for anything unexpected. A diff that applies but changes nothing returns diff_does_not_apply. An unknown report is a plain 404 {detail}, like the other routes.
3. Push failures: non-fast-forward, "fetch first" and "already exists" map to 409 branch_exists (a race after ls-remote). Every other push failure is 502 (SC4).

Verification:
- Full suite: 306 passed, 0 skipped (uv run pytest, local macOS, git 2.54, working tree on ede1dd1). Of these, 55 are in tests/test_open_pr.py. None skipped, so git-http-backend was present.
- Harness as specified: a real bare repo behind an auth-enforcing git http-backend server that records requests, and an httpx MockTransport for GitHub. The analysis clone's origin is an unreachable SSH URL in every test. The teardown of every test asserts SC6, SC7c/d, SC9 and SC10: clone HEAD, branches, status, FETCH_HEAD, config and remotes byte-identical; no refs/bugalizer/*; no worktree; no force argv except the exact worktree-remove argv; every fetch carries --no-write-fetch-head; every remote argv names the canonical URL and carries the env credential; no request unauthorized; the sentinel token absent from responses, captured logs, argv and .git config files.
- Mutation check, run by hand to show the invariants bite. Each of these fails the tests: dropping --no-write-fetch-head, pushing to origin, adding --force to the push, putting the token in the URL, disabling redaction.
- Not verified: CI has not run, because nothing is committed or pushed; committing is Jack's call. open-pr-smoke.ps1 has not been run or parse-checked, because pwsh is not installed here. BOWIE acceptance (SC14) is Greg's post-merge step.

REQUEST_CHANGES — two reproduced claim-lifecycle defects.

1. [P1] Keep claim rollback private to the owner (src/bugalizer/models.py:59; api/reports.py:197; git_ops/pull_request.py:421). Adding FIX_APPROVED -> FIX_PROPOSED to VALID_TRANSITIONS also makes the public PATCH /reports/{id}/status accept that transition, since fix_proposed is an allowed phase target. Reproduced with a live registered claim: PATCH returns 200, changes the row to fix_proposed, and the owner's release_claim CAS then fails. A second open-pr can now replace the token and active registry entry because the registry is checked only when DB status is fix_approved. The original request can still push/open a PR but cannot finalize it. Keep the rollback transition internal, reject external status changes out of the open-pr claim, and check active ownership independently of DB status. Add an API concurrency regression holding the first request mid-flight, attempting the PATCH and a second open-pr, then verifying one owner and successful finalization.

2. [P1] Drain running git work before cleanup and claim release on cancellation (src/bugalizer/git_ops/pull_request.py:476-500 and _run_claimed's to_thread calls). Cancelling an await of asyncio.to_thread does not stop its thread/subprocess. The finally block immediately starts _cleanup, then releases the project lock and report claim while _build_commit or _push is still running. Reproduced by blocking the build thread and cancelling the task: cleanup executes while that thread is live, the report becomes fix_proposed, and the registry entry is removed before the worker exits. This can delete a live worktree or let a retry reuse its path/ref while the old worker still mutates it (or pushes). Retain ownership and the project lock until any dispatched git worker finishes, then clean up and release; account for cancellation during cleanup too. Add a deterministic cancellation test with thread barriers, including the push boundary, proving no overlap with cleanup or a retry.

Verification: accepted the lead's recorded full-suite result (306 passed, 0 skipped); did not rerun it. Two isolated reviewer probes using the submitted Harness passed in 3.27s, demonstrating the defects above (/tmp/test_open_pr_review.py); no implementation or repository test files edited. Read the implementation, DB/route/model changes, approved plan, and test harness. No arbiter interjections.

Before approval, also supply the full-suite CI evidence at the submitted commit required by SC13 (currently explicitly unverified). Use the contract's one-run budget for the revised submission. The BOWIE acceptance walk remains the explicitly post-merge SC14 step, not a prerequisite for this review.

Reviewed the implementation diff against ede1dd12e15093c94203f52bbde753ff2ccf29db and the approved r3 plan. No arbiter interjections were present. Two correctness fixes are required:

1. [P2] Keep the rollback transition private to the claim owner. src/bugalizer/models.py:59 adds FIX_APPROVED -> FIX_PROPOSED to VALID_TRANSITIONS, and FIX_PROPOSED is already a permitted public target. Consequently PATCH /reports/{id}/status can move a live open-pr request back to fix_proposed. open_pull_request only checks _active_claims when the observed status is fix_approved (pull_request.py:421-425), so a second request then replaces the first request's claim_token and registry entry while it is still running. The first request can still push and POST a PR before its final DB CAS discovers that ownership was lost. Reproduced with the real status route function and DB: hold the first claimed request, PATCH to fix_proposed succeeds, start a second request, and the token changes before the first finishes. Reject public rollback of this internal claim, enforce the live registry check independently of report status, and add a concurrent regression covering this sequence. Audit other public status mutations of a claimed report as part of the fix.

2. [P2] Do not clean up or release ownership until the git worker has stopped. src/bugalizer/git_ops/pull_request.py:476-500 and the asyncio.to_thread calls in _run_claimed: cancellation of the awaiting coroutine does not stop the underlying thread/subprocess. The current finally immediately runs _cleanup, releases the project lock and DB claim, and removes the active registry entry while _build_commit or _push can still be executing. This can remove an in-use worktree, leave refs/worktrees created after cleanup, or let a retry overlap a still-running push. Reproduced by blocking _build_commit in its worker thread and cancelling the request: cleanup ran, the report returned to fix_proposed, and the registry entry disappeared before the worker exited. Preserve ownership and the lock until the worker has finished (or explicitly terminate and reap its subprocess), then clean up; merely shielding a coroutine without awaiting its completion on cancellation is insufficient. Add deterministic cancellation regressions during build and push, including retry and cleanup invariants.

Verification: accepted the lead's reported full suite of 306 passed / 0 skipped; did not rerun the full suite. Two temporary focused reproduction tests at /private/tmp/test_open_pr_review.py passed (they assert the defective behavior described above), using PYTHONPATH=src:tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest /private/tmp/test_open_pr_review.py -q -o asyncio_mode=auto. Git/network operations were stubbed in these reproductions; no remote writes were made and implementation files were not edited. CI at the submitted commit, PowerShell validation, and BOWIE acceptance remain unverified as disclosed by the lead; BOWIE is the planned post-merge acceptance step.

Impl r2 for open-pr. It addresses both P1 findings and adds the SC13 CI evidence. Commit 5ad091f is on phase-8/open-pr, pushed with Jack's approval; no PR is open. There were no interjections.

1. [P1] Claim rollback is private to its owner.
   - models.py: new CLAIM_STATUSES = {FIX_APPROVED}. validate_transition(enforce_phase_gating=True) refuses any transition out of a claim state, so PATCH /status cannot take a report out of fix_approved. FIX_APPROVED -> FIX_PROPOSED stays valid only with enforce_phase_gating=False, which is release_claim's token CAS.
   - pull_request.py: open_pr_running(report_id) (the registry) is checked before the status branch, so a live owner answers in_progress whatever the row says.
   - api/reports.py: DELETE /reports/{id} answers 409 while a claim is live. Soft delete was the other external way to change the status of a claimed row.
   - Test test_live_claim_cannot_be_patched_deleted_or_taken (ASGI, first request held in its fetch worker): PATCH gets 409, a second open-pr gets 409 in_progress, DELETE gets 409. Mid-flight the row is still fix_approved with the owner's token. The first request then returns 201 and the report ends fix_committed, with 1 push and 1 POST. Also test_claim_rollback_is_internal_only.

2. [P1] Cancellation drains git workers.
   - pull_request.py: new `_in_thread` replaces every asyncio.to_thread. It shields the worker and, on cancellation, keeps awaiting it (absorbing repeated cancels) until the thread exits, then re-raises CancelledError. The post-call cleanup in `finally` also runs through `_in_thread`. So the project lock, the claim and the registry entry are held until every dispatched worker, cleanup included, has finished. Only then is the claim released and the entry deregistered.
   - Test test_cancellation_waits_for_the_git_worker[apply|push]: a threading.Event holds the worker after `git apply` or after the real `git push`, and then the task is cancelled. While the worker is held, the test asserts: no new git call starts (no cleanup), the report is fix_approved, the claim is registered, and a retry gets in_progress. After release: CancelledError, every `worktree remove` starts after the held worker's end event, and the report is back at fix_proposed and deregistered. Then a retry returns 201. On the push boundary that retry resumes with no second push and one POST.
   - Both new test groups fail on r1's code. I checked this by reverting each fix on its own: plain to_thread gives 2 failed; a public rollback with a status-gated registry check gives 2 failed.

Verification:
- CI: https://github.com/jblacketter/bugalizer/actions/runs/35299043886, success at 5ad091f1: 310 passed, 0 skipped (the git-http-backend tests ran on Ubuntu).
- Local full suite, one run on the same tree before the commit: 310 passed, 0 skipped.
- Still unverified: open-pr-smoke.ps1 has not been run or parse-checked (no pwsh on this Mac). SC14 BOWIE acceptance is post-merge.

Approved at 5ad091f1cc3f75cce6e20d9dd340cbb664c20be8.

Both r1 P1 findings are addressed. Public transition validation refuses leaving FIX_APPROVED, the registry check is independent of the row status, and the delete route also rejects a live owner. The cancellation wrapper shields and drains dispatched git workers before cleanup, lock release, and claim release; final cleanup uses the same wrapper. Reviewed the new API concurrency and apply/push cancellation regression tests, including successful retry after the push boundary.

Verification: confirmed GitHub Actions run 35299043886 succeeded for the exact submitted HEAD (Ubuntu, Python 3.12). Accepted the recorded result of 310 passed, 0 skipped; did not rerun the full suite or duplicate the focused tests. No arbiter interjections. No implementation edits.

SC14 remains the explicitly post-merge BOWIE acceptance walk. The Windows smoke script has not been run or parse-checked on this Mac, as disclosed by the lead. Approval does not claim that operational acceptance is complete.

Reviewed the implementation diff against ede1dd12e15093c94203f52bbde753ff2ccf29db at HEAD 5ad091f1cc3f75cce6e20d9dd340cbb664c20be8 and the approved plan. No arbiter interjections. The worker-draining cancellation fix addresses the previous lifecycle finding, and the status-independent registry check prevents a second live open-pr owner. One claim-protection race remains.

[P1] Make public status mutation atomic with the claim check (src/bugalizer/api/reports.py:221-232,500-504; src/bugalizer/db.py:552-584). PATCH and DELETE are synchronous routes running in worker threads. Their validation/registry checks happen separately from an unconditional SQL UPDATE. A PATCH can validate fix_proposed -> triaged, or DELETE can observe no active owner, then pause before its database write. An open-pr request can now claim the row; resuming the public request overwrites fix_approved despite the new guards. The open-pr request continues through push and PR POST, then its finalization CAS fails. No PR is recorded, the report remains triaged/rejected with the stale token, and ordinary open-pr retries fail wrong_status. A single-process deployment does not prevent this thread interleaving.

Reproduced both orderings with real ASGI routes and SQLite in /private/tmp/test_open_pr_r2_review.py: hold the public route immediately before report_update_status/report_delete, start open-pr and hold its build worker after claim acquisition, release the public mutation, then release the build. PATCH returns 200 / DELETE 204; the row changes out of fix_approved; the stubbed push and PR POST both execute; open-pr returns 409 in_progress and recorded_pull_request remains absent. Both probes passed (asserting this defective behavior). Git and GitHub were stubbed; no external writes were made.

Use a conditional database write/CAS (or shared synchronization covering checks and writes) so a stale public mutation cannot overwrite a newly acquired claim, and map a lost race to 409. Preserve internal worker status transitions. Add deterministic API regressions for PATCH and DELETE beginning BEFORE claim acquisition, in addition to the existing test where they begin after it. Verify the losing mutation is refused and the owner finalizes successfully with one push/PR.

Verification: accepted the lead's reported 310 passed / 0 skipped at this commit and supplied CI run https://github.com/jblacketter/bugalizer/actions/runs/35299043886; did not rerun the full suite. Attempted only tests/test_open_pr.py plus the initial two probes: 23 passed, 38 setup errors because the sandbox denies binding the harness's localhost HTTP server (PermissionError), not an implementation test failure. Reworked the probes to use stubbed git/GitHub: PYTHONPATH=src:tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest /private/tmp/test_open_pr_r2_review.py -q -o asyncio_mode=auto => 2 passed in 1.73s. No implementation or repository test files edited. PowerShell execution remains unverified; SC14 BOWIE acceptance remains the planned post-merge step.

Impl r3 for open-pr. It addresses the r2 P1, the public mutation race; the other r2 reviewer entry had approved. Commit 69eece0 on phase-8/open-pr, pushed. No interjections.

Process note: two codex reviewer turns ran on r2, because the headless and iterm2 watchers were both running. The APPROVE (02:40:58) and the REQUEST_CHANGES (02:42:42) came from separate turns. I treated the finding as authoritative. At Jack's instruction I stopped the headless watcher (pid 68682); iterm2 is the only watcher now.

[P1] Public status mutation is atomic with the claim.
- db.py: report_update_status(..., expected_status=) does its UPDATE with `AND status = ?` and returns None on a lost race. report_delete(..., expected_status=, expected_claim_token=) is a single conditional UPDATE (the separate SELECT-then-UPDATE is gone) and returns False when no row matched. Both new parameters are keyword-only and optional, so the internal pipeline callers (orchestrator, triage, fix_proposer) are unchanged.
- api/reports.py: PATCH /status passes the status it validated, `current`. On a lost race it answers 409 ("Report status changed during the update"). DELETE reads the row (404 when missing or already deleted), refuses a live claim (409), then deletes only if the status and claim token are still the ones it read, else 409. Checking the token covers an abandoned fix_approved claim that open-pr adopts between the read and the write.
- Test test_public_mutation_started_before_the_claim_cannot_overwrite_it[patch|delete], through the real ASGI routes and SQLite. The public route is held after validation, right before its DB write. open-pr then claims the row and is held in its fetch worker. The public write is released: 409, and the row is still fix_approved with the owner's token and no resolution_reason. Then the build is released: 201, fix_committed, 1 push, 1 PR POST. Both parametrizations fail on 69eece0's routes with the CAS arguments removed (checked by hand, 2 failed); they pass with them. The existing test for a mutation that starts after the claim still passes.

Verification: CI https://github.com/jblacketter/bugalizer/actions/runs/35300561303, success at 69eece07: 312 passed, 0 skipped. That is the one full-suite run for this submission; I did not also run it locally. Still unverified: open-pr-smoke.ps1 (no pwsh here), and SC14 BOWIE acceptance, which is post-merge.

Approved at 69eece077a9400b2da52f17fbfabc703f7f66228.

Reviewed the later round-2 REQUEST_CHANGES alongside the earlier approval, then reviewed the implementation delta from 5ad091f. The remaining public mutation race is addressed: PATCH conditions its write on the validated status; DELETE conditions its write on both the observed status and claim token. A lost race returns 409 without changing the claimed row. The token comparison also protects adoption of an abandoned claim. Optional keyword arguments preserve existing internal pipeline callers.

Reviewed both deterministic API regression cases for public mutation beginning before claim acquisition, including the final owner success and one push/PR assertions. The existing tests cover mutation beginning after acquisition and cancellation boundaries.

Confirmed GitHub Actions run 35300561303 succeeded at the exact submitted HEAD. Accepted the recorded 312 passed, 0 skipped; did not rerun the suite. No arbiter interjections and no implementation edits. Noted the lead's explanation of the duplicate round-2 reviewer dispatches and removal of the headless watcher.

The Windows smoke script remains unexecuted/unparsed locally; SC14 BOWIE acceptance remains the explicitly post-merge operational step. This approval does not claim that acceptance is complete.
